differences.title: 1. TRANSPORT PROTOCOL
differences.leftDesc: Apache Thrift is transport-agnostic, supporting TCP, HTTP, and in-memory transports, offering flexibility in network communication strategies.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC mandates HTTP/2 for its transport layer, leveraging features like multiplexing, header compression, and bidirectional streaming.

differences.title: 2. CONTRACT DEFINITION
differences.leftDesc: Thrift uses its own IDL to define services and data structures, generating code for various languages.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC primarily uses Protocol Buffers (`.proto` files) for defining services and message structures, facilitating cross-language compatibility.

differences.title: 3. COMMUNICATION STYLE
differences.leftDesc: Thrift excels at standard RPC, where clients make direct method calls to remote services.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC supports unary, client-streaming, server-streaming, and bidirectional-streaming RPCs, enabling more complex communication patterns.

differences.title: 4. DATA FORMATS
differences.leftDesc: Thrift offers multiple serialization formats, including Binary and Compact, allowing trade-offs between size and speed.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC uses Protocol Buffers' efficient binary serialization format, optimized for size and performance.

differences.title: 5. BROADER ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Thrift has a long history with strong support in languages like Java, Python, and C++, widely used in older systems.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC benefits from Google's backing, extensive tooling, and a rapidly growing community, especially in microservices.

differences.title: 6. COMMUNITY & GOVERNANCE
differences.leftDesc: Managed under the Apache Software Foundation, Thrift has a stable, community-driven development model.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC is a CNCF graduated project, indicating strong community adoption and robust governance within a major cloud-native ecosystem.

differences.title: 7. PLUGGABLE TRANSPORTS
differences.leftDesc: Thrift's transport abstraction allows integration with custom or specialized transport layers beyond standard network protocols.
differences.rightDesc: gRPC's reliance on HTTP/2 simplifies implementation but limits transport flexibility for non-standard networking needs.
